rationale: The assistant correctly hit the critical safety stop in one turn: 'stop using the hob, including the other rings, and isolate it at the cooker switch or consumer unit', explained the live-parts/liquid-ingress risk, and explicitly ruled out the unsupported options (tape, glue, other rings). It stayed faithful to the single customer message, invented nothing, and appropriately deferred the replace-glass-vs-whole-hob question to an engineer. It asked no follow-up questions, so it did not elicit the crack size/location, model, or raise the home-insurance accidental-damage route, which would have made the escalation more useful; otherwise a well-calibrated, safe response.
